definition: Cognitive behavioral group therapy is a group form of cognitive behavioral therapy used to treat social anxiety disorder. In the source packet, it is described as a well-established and effective in-person psychological treatment that uses standard CBT elements such as exposure to feared situations.

reasons: The claim that cognitive behavioral group therapy uses standard CBT elements such as exposure to feared situations is not directly supported for CBGT in the packet; the exposure example is stated for internet-based CBT, not CBGT.
The wording is partly meta-referential (“In the source packet”) rather than a standalone dictionary definition.

The definition relies on a source-specific effectiveness claim (“well-established and effective”) that is historical study language and should not be presented as current clinical consensus without qualification.

The definition claims that the in-person form “uses standard CBT elements such as exposure to feared situations,” but the packet only explicitly describes this “exposure to feared situations” component in the context of the Internet-based CBT (ICBT) having the same components as conventional CBT—not specifically for CBGT.
